badge.name: Data Guardian
badge.description: Keeps people, data and budgets safe.

card.title: Stay in control
lines: Important actions → a human approves first
Use official sources + user sign-in for permissions
No confidential data in broadly shared agents
Test first, then share with a small group
Watch credits on the agent's Monitor page

steps.title: You are the pilot
steps.text:
- **Approvals (human in the loop)** – before important or irreversible actions, such as orders, payments or emails to many people, a person approves.
- **Permissions** – with user sign-in, the agent answers only from what that person is allowed to see.
- **Data** – never put confidential data, like salaries or health data, into an agent everyone can use.
- **Sharing** – test first, then share with a small pilot group, then expand.
- **Admin guardrails** – your IT admins set policies, for example which connectors are allowed.
- **Costs** – agents use **Copilot Credits**. Your admin assigns credits; you can see your agent's usage on its **Monitor** page.

cards.text: Upload the full salary list so the agent can answer pay questions for everyone
cards.why: Confidential data in a shared agent – anyone could ask for it.

cards.text: Use the official HR SharePoint site as knowledge, with user sign-in
cards.why: Official source, and people only see what they are allowed to see.

cards.text: Let the agent email all 2,000 customers without anyone checking
cards.why: High-impact action with no human approval.

cards.text: A manager approves supply orders over €500 before they are sent
cards.why: Human in the loop for important actions.

cards.text: Share your untested agent with the whole company on day one
cards.why: Test first, then pilot with a small group.

cards.text: Tell the agent to say "I don't know" and link to HR when unsure
cards.why: A clear guardrail beats a confident wrong answer.

steps.question: Approve or block? The agent wants to cancel a supplier contract because of one late delivery.
options: Pause and ask a human to approve first
Cancel and send an apology later
steps.explain: Irreversible, high-impact actions need a **human approval step**.

steps.question: On the GitHub Copilot harness, which of these can use Copilot Credits? (pick all that apply)
options: Building the agent by describing it in natural language
Testing it in the test pane
People chatting with the published agent
Reading Microsoft Learn docs about agents
steps.explain: Building, testing, evaluating **and** running the agent can all use credits. Reading the docs is free 😉

steps.question: Where can you see how many Copilot Credits your agent used?
options: On the agent's Monitor page in Copilot Studio
steps.explain: The **Monitor** page shows your agent's consumption. Your admin sees totals for environments and the tenant, and assigns credits – ask them if you need more.

steps.question: BOSS: Which habit wastes the MOST credits?
options: Writing clear instructions before you start building
Testing a few realistic questions after each change
Re-running the same long test conversation again and again without changing anything
steps.explain: Plan first, then test with purpose. Each run uses credits – repeating identical tests teaches you nothing new.

tips: Add a human approval before irreversible or high-impact actions.
Never put confidential data into a broadly shared agent – instructions are not a lock.
Test, pilot with a small group, then share – and watch credits on the agent's Monitor page.
